minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 25, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:01 p.m., on October 25, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 20, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury

City Council Minutes  1  October 25, 2016
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Ury presented certificates of appreciation to Allison Spivey, Megan Summer, and
  Susan Stinson for volunteer hours at the Animal Services Center; and to Elaine Portnoy for
  volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center. Volunteers
  Christine Dawson, Sharon Packard, Dorothy Rico, and Gloria Romo were unable to attend
  the meeting

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gail Reavis, M.V.: encouraged residents to visit transparentcalifornia.com to find out which public
officials are feeding at the troth. She expressed her disapproval of Mayor Ury’s benefits and that
Mission Viejo Council Members do not have lifetime term limits.

Richard Gardner, Capistrano Beach: introduced himself as a candidate for Municipal Water
District of Orange County, area 7.

Samantha Corwin, Hannah Mayer, and Ruby Hanafy, Girl Scout Troop 3394, M.V.: spoke about
their Girl Scout Troop’s efforts to see that Styrofoam lunch trays are removed from use in
elementary schools in the Saddleback Valley Unified School District:.

Jerry Bryant, M.V.: discussed the rapid growth of apartment houses and stated that there is a
serious problem with the amount of traffic and gridlock that the additional housing and residents
are bringing to the area.

Jan Eisenbeisz, M.V.: announced that she is the owner of Coastal Naturopathic Wellness and a
member of the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce. Ms. Eisenbeisz said that helping people
with preventative healthcare and current health issues is her passion, and her specialties are diet,
nutrition, digestive issues and bioenergetics.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  October 25, 2016
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

5.  Check Register Dated October 14, 2016 in the Amount of $858,525.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2016

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2016

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for August 2016

  Received and filed.

10.  Road Closure Request from Trabuco Hills High School for a 5K Run

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by Trabuco Hills High School authorizing
  the closure of Mustang Run between Los Alisos and Aguilar and a partial closure on
  Empanada on Saturday, June 10, 2017.

11.  Renewal of Letter of Credit Related to Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Variable Rate Demand Revenue Bonds (Mission
  Viejo Mall Improvement Project), 1999 Series A

  Authorized the Executive Director to execute the Letter of Credit Renewal for a Two Year
  Term at a fee of 1.25%.

12.  Ordinances to Ensure Prohibition of all Marijuana Uses in Light of the Potential
  Passage of Proposition 64

  (1) Adopted Ordinance 16-315 a Non-Urgency Ordinance Adding Chapter 11.23B to
  Prohibit Recreational Marijuana Uses in the City to the Fullest Extent Allowed by State
  Law; and (2) adopted Ordinance 16-316 a Non-Urgency Ordinance Replacing Chapter
  11.23 with Chapter 11.23A to Prohibit Medical Marijuana Uses in the City to the Fullest
  Extent Allowed by State Law.
City Council Minutes  3  October 25, 2016
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

*Item 2 was taken out of order.

3.  Check Register Dated September 30, 2016, in the Amount of $1,175,020.67

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to CSM Window and Wood for
  $7,700 worth of repair and replacement at the Melinda House. She asked what preventative
  measures the City takes to stop windows from rotting.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that Melinda
  House was formerly a temporary home sales office and was not built with quality materials.
  The windows were original and were replaced as part of a major repair of the building and
  in an effort to bring it up to today’s standards.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated October 7, 2016, in the Amount of $1,748,603.08

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment to RJM Design Group for a master plan
  for the “lake loop.”

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay said that he is working
  with the Lake Mission Viejo Association and RJM to look at possible aesthetic
  enhancements and viewing areas along Olympiad Road for the heavily used and very
  popular exercise route that goes around the lake.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2016
City Council Minutes  4  October 25, 2016
   Council Member Schlicht asked when the Housing Authority will get an infusion of cash
  as the balance is down to around $400,000.00.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that the cash flow will increase
  soon with expected payments. She also said the low balance was intentional as the City is
  continuing to make payments on the Site C property from the Housing Authority account.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

2.  City Council Minutes

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum noted that on page 13 of the Minutes the street name is wrong
  where the Presbyterian Church of the Master is referenced. It should say Marguerite and
  Oso Parkways, not Marguerite and Alicia Parkways.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of October 12, 2016, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

13.  MV Shuttle-ADA Complementary Paratransit Plan

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ury opened the public hearing at 6:48 p.m. and upon hearing no requests to speak,
  he closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt
  the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Complementary Paratransit Plan associated
  with the City’s fixed route local transit service (MV Shuttle).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  5  October 25, 2016
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

14.  Alicia Parkway Slope Renovation

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Member’s questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) approve
  Contract Amendment #17 in the amount of $10,000 to West Coast Arborist for additional
  trimming and selected removal of trees along Alicia Parkway in the next phase of slopes
  renovations; (2) approve Contract Amendment #3 in the amount of $100,000 to WM
  Vandergeest Landscape Care Inc., along Alicia Parkway in the next phase of slope
  renovations; (3) approve Contract Amendment #3 in the amount of $110,000 to AC
  Landscape for irrigation retrofits and controller installation and (4) adopt Resolution 16-
  50 Amending the Fiscal Year 2016/2017 Operating Budget To Appropriate General Fund
  Reserves For Slope Renovations Along Alicia Parkway.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that traffic is up and revenue is up on both toll roads.
  He also discussed the potential for a 241/91 flyover which could take seven years to
  complete.

16.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report concurrently with item 15 (see above.)

17.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury stated that he had nothing to report.

18.  Update On CUSD Bond Measure Issue

City Council Minutes  6  October 25, 2016
   City Attorney Bill Curley announced that CUSD has been very quiet and although they
  threatened litigation, nothing has been filed against the City or the Mayor personally.

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney Curley discussed cases that his office is working on including the writing of
ordinances, planning activities for land use actions to preserve the status quo, and stray contract
and land use work. He also answered Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum’s questions regarding the City’s
lawsuit against Council Member Schlicht for the illegal parking of her RV.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths reminded residents that the City has a smartphone app called AccessMV.
He and his neighbor recently tested it by submitting a picture of a crack in their sidewalk and the
sidewalk was repaired within four days. He also noticed that there were no doggie bags at his
neighborhood park so he took a picture, submitted it through the app, and the doggie bags were
replaced the next day. Council Member Raths said the app works very well and recommended that
residents download it. He also announced that the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce has really
taken off. They meet every Tuesday morning for a networking breakfast at High Park Tap House
and next Tuesday, November 1 from 7:30 a.m. to 9:30 a.m., Senator Pat Bates will be the guest
speaker.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that the library has been holding a photography competition
for the past 6 or 7 years and he attended the awards ceremony this year. One of the topics that
came up that evening was the idea of using the Potocki Center as an arts venue and he said it got
tremendous applause and the crowd thought it was a wonderful idea. He asked the City Manager
to let him know how to proceed in looking at the concept, regardless of what the Vision Plan turns
out to be. Council Member Sachs noted that he is on the Orange County Fire Authority Board of
Directors and he gets a text message when there are fires or incidences in the City of Mission
Viejo. In the last 45 days there has been a lot of activity and one incident, in particular, was arson.
He said that the Orange County Sheriff’s Department and the Fire Authority quickly apprehended
the perpetrator and he is also amazed at how quickly fires are put out. Council Member Sachs
thanked both the Chief of Police Services and the Orange County Fire Authority for the great work
they’ve been doing in the City. He also talked about the launching of the new MV Shuttle and he

City Council Minutes  7  October 25, 2016
 requested that a sign with the schedule be installed at each bus stop. Council Member Sachs said
that people are using the bus and the compliments from the public have been very, very positive.

Council Member Schlicht

20.  Civic Core Area Vision Plan Process: Concerns as to Process and Scope of Land-Use
  Planning and Regulations

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to reject The Kosmont Opportunity Sites until
  the council answers policy questions on Mixed-Use Housing, Zoning Incentives, Financial
  Incentives and CEQA Process Review. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Council Member Schlicht presented her agenda report.

Council Member Schlicht reminded staff that she had a question at the last meeting regarding a
payment to Eric Winter for drone footage. Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
Keith Rattay responded that staff hired Mr. Winter to make a drone footage inventory all of the
City’s open channels for a historical record. When the City has dealt with the Federal Emergency
Management Agency (FEMA) for storm damage reimbursement in the past, FEMA has asked for
existing footage. Council Member Schlicht also asked about alternatives for the weed killer
Roundup as residents have expressed concern with its poisonous nature. Mr. Rattay said that
Roundup is only used by those licensed to use it and it is applied very minimally. It is also used
as a last resort after organic products are applied. In closing, Council Member Schlicht said that
she has always considered the position of Council Member a sacred trust. She conducts herself
within her principles and her motto is to govern under the Rule of Law.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum reminded her colleagues of Council Member Schlicht’s statement about
governing under the rule of law yet not following the rule of law with the parking of her RV. She
stated that the Council Members care very much about this City and serve from the position of
being a servant, and that’s all. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked staff to add a report from the Local
Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) and a report from the Southern California Association
of Governments (SCAG) to the agendas so she can keep the Council and residents up to date on
what is happening with those agencies. She also asked staff, on behalf of some residents, how to
report dead trees. Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that
by using the City’s AccessMV phone app, the exact location of the trees is pinpointed for staff and
is very helpful. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum reminded residents that there will be an opportunity for
early voting in the Saddleback Room at City Hall from October 29 through November 7. She also
provided a reminder that the City is looking for restaurants and businesses to feature in its new
phone app. She said that we are living in the digital age and have a phenomenal staff that is always
looking for applications that will help residents and that will promote businesses and restaurants.
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked staff for a brief update on the aquatics complex. Assistant City
Manager/Director of Public Services Rattay responded that a pool heater broke at the recreation
center where the Nadadores were scheduled to train temporarily. The heater has since been
City Council Minutes  8  October 25, 2016
 replaced and the demolition plans are proceeding at this time. In closing, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
thanked the Orange County Fire Authority for the swift work in extinguishing a fire in the El
Dorado homes area. It looked like it could be a real disaster but the firefighters put the fire out
very quickly, there was very little damage to the homes, and the neighbors were very grateful for
the good work.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury stated that the City is looking at an RV situation because it has been continuously
parked and he said accusations are being made that are just part of the political season. The Mayor
concluded his comments by wishing everyone a happy and safe Halloween.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:37 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, November 8, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 8, 2016

City Council Minutes  9  October 25, 2016
